newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian monk plans new peace pilgrimage.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian monk plans new peace pilgrimage.

text.p: A monk known as the "Gandhi of Cambodia" will lead a pilgrimage to former Khmer Rouge guerrilla bases three years after a similar walk was abandoned when two marchers were killed, an aide said on Monday.

Maha Ghosananda's walk will begin on March 20 in Battambang city and head 85 km (50 miles) west to Pailin, the former northwestern headquarters of the Maoist Khmer Rouge which came over to government control last year.
The walkers will also pass through the former rebel base of Phnom Malai before ending their pilgrimage in Banteay Chmaar on April 13, the start of Cambodian New Year, the aide said.
"Before we could not go to Pailin because the Khmer Rouge and government were not reunited, but now they are reunited so the commanders there will support the walk," she told Reuters.
The 73-year-old Maha Ghosananda led a peace march to Pailin with scores of local and foreign pilgrims in April 1994.
But the march had to be abandoned when a nun and a monk were killed in the crossfire between Khmer Rouge guerrillas and government soldiers.

The Khmer Rouge, blamed for the deaths of more than one million people from starvation, disease, execution or overwork during their 1975-79 rule, reneged on a 1991 U.N.-brokered peace pact, boycotted elections in 1993 and have been fighting the government since.
The rebel group has been hit by thousands of defections in recent months.
